title: Runtime: emit prefill/decode + batch efficiency + KV-cache signals required by Standard Cost Model (SCM)
creator: Mateo Alvarez
description:
Background / why
SCM v1 needs request-level signals from the serving runtime to (a) estimate costs deterministically and (b) attribute cost drivers in the explain endpoint. Today we have token metering, but we don’t have a consistent prefill/decode split and the “batching efficiency” signal is not standardized across deployments.

This ticket adds runtime-side instrumentation for:
- prefill vs decode time/counters
- batch efficiency (effective batch size / utilization)
- KV-cache (prefix/KV) hit rate

We must meet overhead budgets and produce stable metric names + tags suitable for the telemetry pipeline (cardinality controls).

References
- Confluence: runtime signals required for cost model ("runtime-signals-required-for-cost-model")
- SCM v1 schema inputs: prefill/decode breakdown, batch_size_effective, kv_cache_hit_rate
- Slack threads: eng-runtime (overhead + sampling), eng-platform (tagging + missing-signal handling)

Scope
1) Prefill/decode split
- Emit per-request (and aggregate) counters for:
  - tokens_prefill (input tokens)
  - tokens_decode (output tokens)
  - latency_prefill_ms
  - latency_decode_ms
- Clarify semantics:
  - latency_prefill_ms covers embedding + first-token compute until first token is available (stream start)
  - latency_decode_ms covers subsequent token generation until completion (stream end)
  - if request is non-streaming, still treat “first token ready” as the same internal boundary
- Ensure this works for chat + completion APIs and for speculative decoding paths (if enabled) with consistent attribution.

2) Batch efficiency
- Emit batch_size_effective as a runtime computed signal per request, defined as:
  - "effective_batch_size" = average number of sequences sharing the decode steps this request participated in (time-weighted)
- Also emit:
  - batch_admission_wait_ms (time waiting in scheduler/admission control)
  - batch_decode_steps (count of decode iterations participated)
- Important: batch_size_effective must be computed post-admission control and reflect actual co-scheduled batch composition (not pre-admission queue size).

3) KV-cache hit rate
- Emit per-request:
  - kv_cache_hit_tokens (tokens served from KV/prefix cache)
  - kv_cache_miss_tokens
  - kv_cache_hit_rate = hit_tokens / (hit_tokens + miss_tokens)
- Semantics:
  - Count only prompt/prefix reuse hits (do not count decode-side reuse across tokens)
  - If cache is disabled for a route/model, emit explicit “cache_mode=disabled” tag and set hit/miss tokens to 0 (avoid NaNs downstream).

Metric/event type and where it lands
We need both:
- A per-request structured event (for SCM attribution/explain), emitted once at request end.
- A small set of aggregate metrics for dashboards (p50/p95 breakdowns and sanity checks).

Proposed per-request event (internal name): runtime.request_summary.v1
Fields (high level):
- request_id (already present in tracing)
- model_id, model_version (from catalog binding)
- deployment_mode: hosted|dedicated|private
- region
- gpu_sku (if known in runtime; otherwise allow unknown and rely on control plane enrichment)
- quant_profile_id (if applied)
- tokens_prefill, tokens_decode
- latency_prefill_ms, latency_decode_ms, latency_total_ms
- batch_size_effective
- batch_admission_wait_ms
- kv_cache_hit_tokens, kv_cache_miss_tokens, kv_cache_hit_rate

Tagging rules (cardinality constraints)
- model_id: allowed
- model_version: allowed only if it is the pinned semantic version (not build hash)
- region: allowed
- gpu_sku: allowed, normalized to Redwood canonical SKU list (e.g., "A100-80GB", "H100-80GB", "L40S")
- route_id: NOT allowed on aggregate metrics by default (too high cardinality); allowed in per-request events only.
- tenant_id: NOT emitted from runtime; enrichment/joins happen downstream in control plane telemetry where access controls exist.

Performance / overhead budgets
Hard constraints:
- CPU overhead in runtime process: < 0.5% at p95 throughput load (decode-heavy workload)
- Added latency: < 0.2ms per request (median) and < 1ms at p99 under synthetic load
- Allocation budget: no per-token allocations; aggregate counters should be stack-local and flushed once at end-of-request
- Sampling: request_summary events may be sampled for high-QPS tenants in hosted, but must support “force on” for canary/diagnostics

Implementation plan
- Add counters to scheduler + decode loop:
  - start_prefill_ts, end_prefill_ts
  - decode_start_ts, decode_end_ts
  - batch composition snapshots (for time-weighted effective batch size)
- Thread-safe aggregation:
  - attach per-request metrics object to request context
  - update in tight loops using plain integer/f64 increments (no locks)
  - flush on completion to telemetry exporter
- KV cache:
  - record hit/miss tokens at cache lookup layer
  - ensure we can distinguish "cache disabled" vs "cache enabled but cold"
- Backward/rollout:
  - gated by feature flag: runtime.emit_scm_signals_v1
  - default off in prod until telemetry pipeline is ready (ENG-23155)

Acceptance criteria
- Prefill/decode split is available in runtime.request_summary.v1 for 99%+ of requests (excluding known early-termination failures).
- batch_size_effective matches offline validation (unit + integration tests) within 1% relative error on deterministic test harness.
- KV cache hit rate aligns with cache layer logs on test workload (within 0.5% absolute difference).
- Overhead budgets met, with documented benchmark results + flamegraph notes.
- Metric/tag names reviewed and approved by Telemetry (Logan/Nadia) and SCM platform owner (Priya).

Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - boundary conditions (0 decode tokens, short prompts, streaming vs non-streaming)
  - cache disabled and partial hit cases
  - batch_size_effective calculation on synthetic scheduler traces
- Integration tests:
  - staging: emit events and verify ingestion to telemetry pipeline (behind flag)
- Perf tests:
  - run runtime perf harness on decode-heavy prompt set; compare baseline vs instrumentation-on

Notes / open questions
- Speculative decoding: do we attribute prefill/decode split to the “winning” tokens only, or include speculative work? Proposal: include all compute in latency fields (actual work), but token counters reflect finalized tokens. SCM can treat this via assumptions.
- Retries/fallback: if runtime restarts mid-stream, can we emit partial summaries? Proposal: emit best-effort with "completion_status=partial" field (optional) and allow SCM confidence to drop.

Deliverables
- Runtime emits runtime.request_summary.v1 behind feature flag
- Aggregates: runtime_prefill_latency_ms, runtime_decode_latency_ms, runtime_batch_size_effective (histograms)
- Short internal doc snippet with field definitions + examples for telemetry team
comments: 2025-02-04 (Omar El-Sayed): Drafted event schema + tagging proposal. Biggest risk is batch_size_effective correctness; I’m going to implement time-weighted average based on scheduler snapshots at decode steps, not queue size.

2025-02-06 (Sofia Ivanova): Please ensure batch_size_effective is computed after admission control. We’ve had confusion where pre-admission queue length was reported as “batch size”. Also, for streaming requests, boundary is “first token ready”, not “HTTP headers sent”.

2025-02-07 (Logan Wright): Re: tags—do not include route_id on aggregate metrics. OK in per-request events (sampling + access controls downstream). Prefer gpu_sku normalized; if runtime doesn’t know it, emit unknown and let control plane enrich.
2025-02-10 (Nadia Rahman): KV cache hit rate semantics look good. Please emit explicit cache_mode=disabled when cache is turned off; downstream math breaks with nulls/NaNs.

2025-02-12 (Omar El-Sayed): Implemented counters and exporter wiring behind runtime.emit_scm_signals_v1. Perf harness shows +0.12ms median overhead, p99 +0.6ms; CPU +0.3% at target load. Posting flamegraph in PR.
2025-02-14 (Mateo Alvarez): Reviewed boundary semantics. Please add a unit test for 0-decode-token requests (e.g., max_tokens=0) to avoid negative decode timing.

2025-02-18 (Omar El-Sayed): Fixed bug: batch_size_effective was computed using batch size at enqueue (pre-admission). Now computed from actual co-scheduled batch composition. Added regression test and updated docstrings.
2025-02-21 (Priya Natarajan): Approved. Marking Done. Next: telemetry pipeline dimension support + SCM service consumption (ENG-23155 / ENG-23128).
